```{r}
#| include: false

```

`mizu_map()` maps a function over a vector or list on the pool and returns a map handle immediately — as `mizu_submit()` returns a task. `mizu_collect()` on the handle waits and returns the results in input order; `as.promise()` (or `then()` directly) collects through the event loop instead — see [Promises and handlers](pools.html#promises-and-handlers).
It is not a loop over `mizu_submit()`.
The function, its constant arguments, and the data are staged once in shared memory.
A handful of chunk tasks divide the elements, and each worker sets up the map at most once.
The per-element cost approaches the cost of `lapply()`, while the work spreads across workers and balances itself through stealing.

```{r map}
library(mizu)

p <- mizu_pool(n_workers = 4L)
m <- mizu_map(p, 1:5, \(i) i * 2L)
mizu_collect(m)
```

## Templates

A `.template` (in the style of the `FUN.VALUE` argument of `vapply()`) gives you an atomic vector or matrix instead of a list.
The workers write the results straight into shared memory: each result crosses the process boundary exactly once, without serialization:

```{r map-template}
m <- mizu_map(p, seq.int(-5, 5), abs, .template = numeric(1))
mizu_collect(m)
```

With `.collect = "view"`, the result is the shared output area itself, wrapped as a read-only ALTREP view: no final copy, and the region stays alive until the view is garbage collected.

An `integer64` template (bit64's layout, constructed without bit64) is also supported.
An int64 result never widens to double, so results must be exact `integer64` of the template's length.

## Reproducible randomness

Random numbers drawn inside the function are not reproducible by default, and cost nothing extra.
Pass `.seed` to give every element its own L'Ecuyer-CMRG stream.
Then the results are identical for any chunking, worker count, or steal order:

```{r map-seed}
m1 <- mizu_map(p, 1:4, \(i) rnorm(i), .seed = 123L)
m2 <- mizu_map(p, 1:4, \(i) rnorm(i), .seed = 123L, .chunks = 4L)
identical(mizu_collect(m1), mizu_collect(m2))
```

## Prepared maps

`mizu_map_prepare()` stages a map — the function, its constant arguments, and the data — without running it: the serialization and the region creation are paid once.
Each `mizu_map_run()` then costs only task submission and collection, and reuses the map context cached by each worker.
Repeated stochastic simulation is the headline use: `.seed` rides each run rather than the region, so the random streams vary per run for free:

```{r map-prepared}
pm <- mizu_map_prepare(p, 1:1000, \(i, draws) mean(rnorm(draws)) * i, draws = 100L)
runs <- lapply(1:4, \(s) {
  m <- mizu_map_run(pm, .seed = s)
  mizu_collect(m)
})
vapply(runs, \(r) r[[1L]], numeric(1))
```

`mizu_map_run(pm, .x = x2)` replaces the staged data: an atomic vector of the same type and length swaps in place at the cost of one copy; any other replacement restages automatically.
A run collected with `.collect = "view"` hands its region to the view, so the next run restages into a fresh one.
The handle keeps the staged data and the region alive for its lifetime; both release at garbage collection.

## Nested maps

A map can nest: `mizu_map(mizu_current_pool(), ...)` inside a task expression uses the handle of the worker running the task.
The runner submissions push straight onto that worker's own deque, and the blocked collect executes its own runners while idle peers steal the rest: nested maps never deadlock the pool.
A `.template` on the nested map collects as an atomic vector the task reduces directly — no list assembly, no `unlist()`:

```{r map-nested}
t <- mizu_submit(
  p,
  {
    m <- mizu_map(mizu_current_pool(), parts, sum, .template = numeric(1))
    sum(mizu_collect(m))
  },
  parts = split(as.numeric(1:100000), rep(1:10, each = 1e4))
)
mizu_collect(t)
```

The first nested map of a worker claims a submitter slot, so at the default `max_submitters = 8` — one held by the controller — at most 7 workers can nest concurrently.
Raise `max_submitters` for wider nested fan-outs.

```{r map-stop}
mizu_pool_stop(p)
```
